                                        PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING    TO   IMPLEMENT §                             PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION     §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA § 37.0561 §                                         OF TEXAS


 PERMIAN BASIN PETROLEUM ASSOCIATION’S COMMENTS IN RESPONSE TO
            PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION OF 16 TAC § 25.194

TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS:

        The Permian Basin Petroleum Association (PBPA) respectfully files the following

comments in response to the Public Utility Commission of Texas’ (Commission) Proposal for

Publication of 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 25.194 (PFP):

                                            COMMENTS

        PBPA is the largest regional oil and gas association in the United States and has served as

the voice of the Permian Basin oil and gas industry since 1961. Currently, the Permian Basin is

the most prolific oil and gas producing region in the world. More broadly, the oil and gas industry

is a driver of the Texas economy and a major contributor to the country’s national security. As the

leading oil and gas producer globally, the United States relies heavily on the Permian Basin, which

generates nearly half of all oil and gas produced in the United States. Additionally, most of the oil

produced in Texas is produced in the Permian Basin.

        As the Commission is aware, many producers must meet their electrical needs for mineral

development with localized, off-grid combustion generation due to the lack of transmission and

generation capacity in the region. In addition, operators that are grid-connected face the increasing risk

of transmission curtailments — including the curtailment of critical natural gas facilities — due to

Generic Transmission Constraints (GTCs) that ERCOT has issued for the region. 1


        1
         ERCOT Market Notice, W-A090425-01 New Far West Texas Import Generic Transmission Constraints
(GTCs), https://www.ercot.com/services/comm/mkt_notices/W-A090425-01.

                                                                                               Page 1 of 7
        PBPA appreciates the comments by Commissioner Hjaltman that addressed the wide-

reaching effect of this rule on all types of large loads in Texas. PBPA’s members will be directly

and indirectly impacted by the rule. Members with facilities that have loads greater than 75

megawatts (e.g., gas processing plants, refineries, etc.) will be subject to the proposed rule

requirements. Members with both large loads and smaller loads will be indirectly impacted if the

rule or the batch process at ERCOT allows loads that have been waiting years for interconnection

to be inadvertently superseded in the interconnection process by those utilizing the batch process.

PBPA further urges that the batch study process for large loads should not interrupt or delay

transmission service providers’ processing of interconnection requests and studies for loads under

75 MW.

       PBPA, accordingly, requests that the Commission take steps to ensure the proposed rule

and the ongoing batch process at ERCOT create a timely path to interconnection not only for the

large loads over 75 MW, but for all the loads that supported the Permian Basin Reliability Plan.

PBPA appreciates that ERCOT’s April 4 comments on Planning Guide Revision Request 145

(PGRR145) added the Permian Basin Reliability Plan Study completed by ERCOT in 2024 as a

study considered to be complete and valid under proposed paragraph (3) of Section 9.2.1.4,

Evaluation of Existing Interconnection Studies for Large Loads, since the study was used by the

Commission to establish the need for certain transmission projects. Proposed Section 9.2.1.4,

Evaluation of Existing Interconnection Studies for Large Loads, now states:

                       (3) ERCOT shall consider previous studies for Large Loads
               that have not achieved Initial Energization by July 10, 2026, to be
               fully complete and valid without additional review if they meet one
               of the following criteria:

                      (c)     The Large Load was included in the Permian Basin
               Reliability Plan Study completed by ERCOT in 2024 and approved
               by the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) in Docket No.


                                                                                         Page 2 of 7
                 55718, and the Load contributed to establishing the need for the
                identified transmission projects.

PBPA generally supports this language.            However, PBPA requests clarification from the

Commission and ERCOT regarding how large loads and loads under 75 MW that supported the

plan will be treated. For example, because the transmission system is open access and many oil

and gas loads under 75 MW rely on the backbone of the transmission system, it remains unclear

how ERCOT will ensure that oil and gas loads under 75 MW that supported the need for the

Permian Basin Reliability Plan will be able to interconnect as the local and import paths for the

Permian Basin Reliability Plan come online. Ultimately, the Plan was supported by approximately

12 GW of oil and gas related load and another 12 GW of additional load. 2 PBPA requests

clarification from ERCOT and the PUCT on how loads that supported the plan will be treated.

        ERCOT’s April 4 comments on PGRR145 indicate that the Batch Zero process will be the

sole path forward for large load interconnection once PGRR145 is approved, and that large loads

not meeting the Batch Zero eligibility criteria will be ineligible for Initial Energization until

evaluated through a future interconnection study process. As the Commission considers guidance

on the Batch Zero eligibility criteria—as discussed at the Commission’s April 2, 2026 Open

Meeting—PBPA requests that the Commission ensure that the eligibility criteria and any allocation

methodology appropriately account for the loads that supported the Permian Basin Reliability Plan,

including loads under 75 MW that are not directly subject to the proposed rule but that rely on the

backbone transmission system being constructed pursuant to the plan.

        Statutory directives to the Commission from Texas House Bill (HB) 5066, enacted by the 88th

Texas Legislature, support taking steps to ensure that the oil and gas loads that supported the Permian



        2
           PUC Project No. 55718, Reliability Plan for the Permian Basin Under PURA § 39.167, ERCOT Permian
Basin Reliability Plan Study at 6.

                                                                                                Page 3 of 7
 Basin Reliability Plan have sufficient capacity to interconnect as the local and import path lines to the

region come online. Section 39.167 of PURA required the Commission to direct ERCOT to develop a

reliability plan under PURA § 39.166 for the Permian Basin region, which was adopted by the

Commission in PUC Project No. 55718, Reliability Plan for the Permian Basin Under PURA §

39.167. ERCOT’s reliability plan was required to: (1) address extending transmission service to

areas where mineral resources have been found; (2) address increasing available capacity to meet

forecasted load; and (3) provide available infrastructure to reduce interconnection times in areas

without access to transmission service. 3 Legislative history also supports that the background and

purpose of the plan was to improve transmission to serve heavy oil and gas development in West

Texas where the timeline to build transmission was not keeping pace with demand. 4 PBPA,

therefore, respectfully requests the Commission carefully consider how the PFP and Planning

Guide Revision Request (PGRR) 145 process will impact the energization of oil and gas loads and

critical natural gas loads. 5

        PBPA further notes that the Commission’s Second Order in PUC Project No. 55718, issued in

April 2025, approved the three 765-kV import paths identified in the Permian Basin Reliability Plan.

These import paths, together with the common local projects approved in the Commission’s initial

October 2024 Order, represent a generational investment in transmission infrastructure for the Permian

Basin region.    The Permian Basin Reliability Plan Study relied upon load forecasts projecting

approximately 12 GW of oil-and-gas-related load and approximately 12 GW of additional non-oil-and-

gas load in the region by 2030, for a total of approximately 24 GW of forecasted demand. It is therefore

           PUC Project No. 55718, Reliability Plan for the Permian Basin Under PURA § 39.167, Order at 2
(Oct. 5, 2024).
         4
           C.S.H.B 5066, State Affairs, Bill Analysis at 1.
         5
           Proposal for Publication of New 16 TAC § 25.194 at 7 (Mar. 12, 2026) (proposed 16 TAC § 25.194(b))
(PFP).

 critical that the proposed rule and the ongoing PGRR145 Batch Zero process include appropriate

safeguards to ensure that this transmission infrastructure is made available to serve oil and gas loads

that formed a substantial basis for the plan and justified the need for these investments.



                                       Respectfully Submitted,

                                        /s/ Ben Shepperd

                                        Ben Shepperd
                                        President
                                        Permian Basin Petroleum Association

 RULEMAKING    TO   IMPLEMENT §                         PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION     §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA § 37.0561 §                                     OF TEXAS



        PERMIAN BASIN PETROLEUM ASSOCIATION’S EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

         PBPA submits these comments to ensure that the Commission’s proposed rule under 16

TAC § 25.194 and ERCOT’s ongoing PGRR145 Batch Zero process do not inadvertently

undermine the objectives of the Permian Basin Reliability Plan adopted by the Commission in

PUC Project No. 55718. The Permian Basin Reliability Plan—including the three 765-kV import

paths and common local projects—was developed and approved to address longstanding

transmission deficiencies in the Permian Basin, with approximately half of the region’s forecasted

load attributable to oil and gas operations.     PBPA’s core concern is that this generational

transmission investment must timely and adequately serve the oil and gas loads that justified the

plan.


         PBPA’s comments and recommendations can be summarized as follows:


         1.    PBPA supports ERCOT’s recognition in the April 4, 2026 PGRR145 comments that

loads included in the Permian Basin Reliability Plan Study that contributed to establishing the need

for transmission projects should be considered as having a complete and valid study for purposes

of the Batch Zero process.


         2.    PBPA requests clarification from the Commission and ERCOT on how large loads

that supported the plan and oil and gas loads under 75 MW—which are not directly subject to the

proposed rule but which rely on the backbone transmission system being constructed pursuant to


                                                                                          Page 6 of 7
 the plan—will be treated under the Batch Zero process and in future interconnection study

processes.


          3.     PBPA requests that the Commission direct ERCOT to preserve sufficient transmission

capacity on the local and import path projects approved in PUC Project No. 55718 for oil and gas

loads—including loads under 75 MW—that supported the need for those projects, and to periodically

reassess whether actual and projected load growth is consistent with the load forecasts relied upon in

the Permian Basin Reliability Plan.


          4.     PBPA urges the Commission to consider the unique statutory context of the Permian

Basin Reliability Plan under PURA §§ 39.166-39.167 and HB5066, which specifically directed

the Commission to address extending transmission service to areas of mineral resource

development and increasing available capacity to meet forecasted load in the Permian Basin

region.


          PBPA appreciates the Commission’s consideration of these comments and stands ready to

participate in further proceedings to ensure the Permian Basin Reliability Plan achieves its

intended purpose of providing reliable and sufficient transmission infrastructure for all loads in the

region, including the oil and gas loads that are fundamental to the Texas economy and national

energy security.
